steps.description: Alchemix treats `yield tokens` (`ERC-4626` vault shares, interest-bearing tokens, etc.) via small plug-ins called adapters. Each adapter obeys the `ITokenAdapter` interface so the rest of the protocol can ask a simple question: “how many underlying tokens does one share represent right now?” We will walk through the interface and then see how the concrete `EulerUSDCAdapter` fulfils it.
version() (line 9) returns a short semantic-version string so core contracts know which implementation they are talking to.
token() (line 14) exposes the address of the yield token (the ERC-4626 share or interest-bearing token) governed by this adapter.
underlyingToken() (line 19) tells the caller which plain ERC-20 asset backs the yield token.
price() (line 25) is the crucial hook: it must return the amount of underlying redeemable for exactly 1 whole yield token.
Now let’s see how the concrete adapter for `Euler’s USDC vault` implements those requirements.
line 11 defines a public constant version = "1.0.0" – this is what version() will implicitly return through Solidity’s public-constant getter, satisfying the first interface function.
Lines 13-15 declare immutable token and underlyingToken.  Once written in the constructor, the addresses cannot change, so every price() call refers to the same vault share and its underlying USDC.
The constructor (lines 17-20) captures those addresses at deployment, wiring the adapter permanently to a specific Euler eUSDC vault and to USDC as its underlying.

price() implementation (lines 22-24):
1. Calls `IERC4626(token).convertToAssets(10**TokenUtils.expectDecimals(token))` – i.e. converts exactly one share (1 × 10^decimals) into the amount of underlying `USDC`.
2. Relies on the **ERC-4626** vault’s up-to-date conversion logic, so the result moves with accumulated interest.
`price()` needs the share’s decimals so that **"one whole token"** is converted. That information comes from `TokenUtils.expectDecimals`.

`expectDecimals()` (lines 26-34) performs a low-level staticcall to the **ERC-20**’s `decimals()` selector and decodes the `uint8` value, reverting if the call fails. The adapter uses this helper to remain safe and generic across tokens with different decimal counts.

Putting it together: any Alchemix component that needs the live price of the Euler `eUSDC` yield token just calls `EulerUSDCAdapter.price()`. The adapter forwards to the vault’s `convertToAssets` logic, scales for decimals, and returns the precise USDC-per-share ratio – all through the common `ITokenAdapter` abstraction.
